issues.description: Single full original 1647 copy only; no independent manuscript or edition collated.
The p381 house-of-thief / door material follows AFTER the declared B02u phase stop, starts next source batch on same physical page; original page image already preserved.
Full Lilly Chapter L continues beyond p381 through original PDF400, and the accepted index must remain PARTIAL after B02u.
Three original page overlaps 369/373/377 require semantic de-duplication; count once, preserve excluded source-reader draft units.
Printed p339 six zodiac classifications are represented separately after original-source review, not independently observed six cases.
The old text alleges thief identity, gender, social roles, guilt, clothing and names without verifiable evidence; never identify a real criminal or give legal enforcement advice.
The printed name table on PDF375 has companion glyphs and blank slots; extracted page/table units are not certified individual diplomatic transcriptions of every cell.
Original printing, same-volume errata and later handwritten marks are separate witnesses; damaged p3?7 locator is not confidently p337.
Original ancient authority attributions are Lilly-mediated; underlying Al-Kindi/other external sources not independently collated.
No original individual suspect charts, birth data, crime records, successful predictions or calibrated probability evidence are supplied.
Different rules for ascendant ruler, seventh ruler, Moon and hour ruler cannot be freely substituted between source subheadings.
Source may contain contradictory fixed/immovable and multiple-thief sign classifications; retain rather than silently harmonize.
Historical positions, distance/house/furlong scales and directions lack modern calibrated map or ephemeris validation.
Source name/gender/race/occupation appearances are period stereotype assertions, not real-world attribute inferencing.
No participant data, synthetic target, blinded forecast, working HumanDesign model or prior source IDs are altered by source-documentary intake.
Original reviewer B/C/D checked page spans but the merged overlap logic and C006 six-row disaggregation are controller changes, not newly independent observational evidence.
Two new clean-context source readers disagree over p332 jest-condition aspect glyph (opposition vs conjunction). It is source-qualified rather than silently assigned a single operator.
Later handwritten numerals, margin 7th-House marks and the p335 'Planet' caret are not authenticated original Lilly print.
P331 exact separate: hour lord identical to seventh lord gives radicality; seventh lord in ascendant under suspicion is a different allegation, not automatically a crime.
An asserted hope of DISCOVERY is not a guaranteed RECOVERY; the source's 'scant be had again' is opposite the earlier bad paraphrase 'soon returned'.

In 'the peregrine Planet give vertue', the definite article can refer back to the preceding peregrine planet in the Ascendant. The candidate's assertion that no house is specified should not settle whether that earlier placement remains inherited.

The 'Not stolen' construction combines 'neither', 'or', and 'separate not', involving the Moon-house lord, second-house lord, and other planets separating from them. Preserve the printed negative construction without imposing a definitive Boolean expansion.
The future-theft passage clearly includes 'or fift', but the reach of 'having her selfe neither' sextile nor trine to house cusps across its destination alternatives remains uncertain.
The subject of 'and have no' sextile or trine to the seventh-house planet is not securely supplied. Preserve the donor, recipient, and negative-aspect relation without assigning the missing subject.

The final body line visibly contains 'Planet' and ends with 'house or'; the next page begins 'of the ☽'. The same-volume errata separately directs 'Planet' at page 335's last line. Its exact replacement target is not demonstrated by that instruction alone, and handwritten marks cannot establish an authorial correction.

The peregrine-planet/Moon virtue exchange is followed by an additional 'if' involving the thief's conjunction, square, or opposition to the Moon, or aspect to the Moon's term lord. The punctuation does not securely determine whether these are cumulative requirements or parallel conditions.

Page 335 assigns missing/not-stolen outcomes to lunar virtue given to Saturn, Mars, cadent planets, or the eighth lord; page 336 assigns overlapping stolen/taken-away outcomes. Both printed rules must remain, including page 336's movable/fixed distinction.
In 'and he in a movable Signe', the antecedent of 'he' and the reach of the movable-sign qualification over the preceding alternatives are uncertain.

The young-person list includes joining Venus, the Moon increasing in light, the first ten degrees or middle of a sign, and the beginning of the Oriental quarter. Its punctuation leaves some subjects and conjunctions unresolved; these conditions must not be turned into a fully specified logical formula.
The later 'immovable, or a double bodied Sign' rule gives more than one thief, while earlier fixed-sign conditions give one. Retain the conflicting print rather than emending immovable to movable.

The locator preceding 'l 28 r for ☉ and ♂' has a faint middle digit. A reading of 307 is plausible; 337 is not securely established. No correction to the supplied page-337 lunar age passage follows from this uncertain locator.

The earlier fixed-sign-and-direct-ascensions rule gives one thief, whereas the later immoveable-sign rule gives more than one. Preserve both printed assertions; the supplied errata contains no correction for printed p339.

The compressed coordination of fixed sign, direct ascensions, few children, and few shapes must retain its printed AND/OR structure. The later mutual-luminary rule does not repeat the square explicitly required by the earlier rule.

The name tables repeat planetary combinations for different names and contain blank joined-planet cells. Preserve every row, its principal significator, its companion glyphs, and its blanks; do not create unique mappings or expand blanks into conditions.

The friendly-aspect clause ends with 'idem' immediately after the overthwart-neighbour result. That immediate antecedent supports the candidate's reading, but the compressed referral should remain visible rather than becoming an independently explicit result.

The opening sentence under 'A Stranger or Familiar' compresses the coordination of luminaries beholding the ascendant, the ascendant's lord in the first, and joining the seventh's lord. Retain the source wording alongside the candidate's contextual parsing.
The triplicity and terms clauses omit a repeated subject. Continuing the luminary subject is contextual. The return rule's plural 'they' does not expressly identify which planets must be retrograde.

The second-house paragraph shifts through 'it' between the alleged person and the lost thing. The attachment of the power-of-the-loser and recovery-by-money clauses should remain qualified rather than silently generalized.
The fourth-house occupational alternative visibly ends 'Labou-' before the next line begins 'of the Land'. Preserve the incomplete printing rather than supplying an unseen suffix.
The fifth-house masculine-sign parenthesis follows the cousin/nephew alternative; its full grammatical scope is uncertain.
The seventh-house paragraph gives wife/lady and other alternatives, then a feminine-sign enemy assertion. Retain both and the printed marginal caution 'This must be warily understood.'
The eighth-house assertion begins with a stranger but ends 'yet seem-' with catchword 'eth'. Its substantive qualification continues outside the supplied window.
The ascendant-OR-fourth rule and the subsequent specific fourth-house alternatives both appear in print. Neither replaces the other.

The second-house paragraph moves from personal alternatives to being within someone's power and recovery by money without explicitly restating the subject or object. Preserve that uncertainty while retaining the power relationship.
The fourth-house paragraph visibly ends a line with 'Labou-' and the following line begins 'of the Land'. The missing word completion is not securely supplied by this image.
The fifth-house masculine-sign parenthesis follows the son-or-daughter-of-cousin-or-nephew alternatives. Its grammatical reach is not explicitly settled.

The seventh-house feminine-sign condition follows the market buyer-or-seller alternative and precedes the enemy assertion. Preserve its position and the printed warning 'This must be warily understood'; do not relocate the condition to harmonize the paragraph.

The eleventh-house paragraph leaves the scope of 'or Neighbour' open and uses the awkward construction 'of the Houshold of the Querent his Mother'. Preserve the wording rather than asserting additional relationships.

The thief-significator distance scale names the ascendant lord in the fixed branch but the ascendant in the common and movable branches. Its movable branch counts terrestrial houses. The separate ascending-sign scale instead assigns half a mile per house when movable. Retain both scales and their differing endpoints and units.
The margin prints 'These judgments best agree from the Country'. Retain the unusual preposition without silently converting it into a precise geographical restriction.

The earlier general angular-placement rule says the thief remains in town, whereas this page distinguishes strong-angular remaining from weak-angular departure and separately gives the square-to-ascendant-lord rule. No precedence or reconciliation is printed.

In the sixth-lord paragraph, the word before 'any of their Lords' resembles 'will' or 'with'. Preserve the uncertain connective; do not invent an aspect, reception, conjunction or application condition.
The margin explicitly associates 'sometimes' with the willing return of goods. Whether it additionally qualifies the adjacent arrival-before-the-querent prediction is uncertain.

The direction methods attributed to others remain separate from the author's preference for the stronger of the significator and Moon. The pronoun in 'to whom he doth apply, or render his power' is not fully resolved, and rendering power is not defined here.
The Taurus glyph is followed by 'in the South against the east', then 'and so of the rest'. Preserve this wording and do not supply a precise bearing or an absent twelve-sign table.

The house-location paragraph first uses the thief's significator, then explicitly assigns the Sun to the house and Moon to its door. These distinct actors must remain distinct; their rules are not unified by the source.

The fourth-sign assignment reads 'where the thing is, that is, or was taken away'. Its awkward wording should remain visible; A1005's definite 'from which' is an interpretation rather than an unambiguous original phrase.

The opening 'his Lord' continues PDF365's 'the querent, and'. Preserve that antecedent context and the uncertainty about the precise subject of 'signifieth the place'; do not introduce an antecedent absent from the preceding page.

The general recovery paragraph lists the Sun, Moon, ascendant lord, second lord, and lord of the Moon's house, their applications, and mutual aspects. Its punctuation does not unambiguously assign a separate aspect target to every listed item.

In the jest rule, opposition is legible, but the grammatical attachment of the opposition and sextile-or-trine clauses remains awkward. Preserve the stated house target without replacing it with an unstated planet.
'Not farre remote' supplies neither a numerical distance nor an explicit reference point.

The page locator in the entry immediately before p312, directing a line-28 correction involving Sun and Mars, is damaged. Do not assert its page number as definite. The clear p335 final-line correction 'Planet' and p336 line-4 and line-9 corrections 'vertue' concern pages outside A1 and must not be applied to printed pages 330–332.
The handwriting establishes neither annotator identity nor date. The small mark associated with the upper-margin 7 should not receive a definite ordinal expansion.
The opening his Lord continues PDF365. Its antecedent cannot be established from the supplied images and must remain unsupplied.
The recovery paragraph's punctuation does not securely delimit every aspect pairing. Preserve the full named list and mutual applications without inventing pairings.
The jest configuration prints conjunction to the second house. Do not silently replace that target with the second-house lord.
The opening reads If ☽ be the seventh, without a clearly printed in. Distinguish the literal wording from an inferred seventh-house reading.
The scope of or the lord of the seventh in the third remains ambiguous within the preceding compound travelling-loss configuration.

The theft-significator sentence supplies square/opposition for the ascendant lord and conjunction/square/opposition for the Moon, then lists further targets without repeating aspect glyphs. Carry-over to those targets is not explicit.
The handwritten numerical sequence's first digit and the separate apparent 4 are less secure than the remaining visible numerals.

The Not stolen paragraph has the awkward double negative neither ... separate not. The candidate's no-separation interpretation is plausible but should remain distinguished from the diplomatic wording.
The unfinished bottom clause appears to end house or; of remains a possible letterform reading. The catchword is the. Neither the completed target nor the conclusion is available.
The handwritten a and caret visibly affect Planet, but the underlying letter and whether the annotation implements the printed errata cannot be certified. Do not infer a replacement of lord.
The later entry ending l 13 dele give has a damaged page locator. Do not assert a definite page number or apply that deletion to any A2 clause.
